title: Lancashire Hotpot
subtitle: Slow-braised lamb with overlapping potato crust
excerpt: Layers of lamb neck chops and onions topped with overlapping potato slices and slowly baked until the meat is tender and the potatoes are golden and crisp on top. The definitive dish of industrial Lancashire.

recipe.sourceNotes: Lancashire hotpot is one of the oldest surviving regional British dishes. It takes its name from the tall, straight-sided brown pottery dish in which it was traditionally cooked. The dish was the practical meal of working-class families in the cotton-mill towns of Lancashire: inexpensive lamb neck chops layered with onions and potatoes, placed in the oven in the morning, and left to cook slowly until the evening meal. Lamb kidneys are traditionally included for extra richness, though many modern versions omit them. The essential quality is the crisp, well-browned potato top that contrasts with the tender, gelatinous meat below. It is served with pickled red cabbage in Lancashire.

recipeTools.notes: A deep oven-proof casserole or hotpot dish, about 2 litres.

content.text: The genius of the hotpot is the potato lid: the slices overlap like roof tiles and spend the first 2 hours cooking covered, steaming in the meat juices, then the lid comes off for the final 30 minutes so the top crisps and browns. Cut the potato slices to a consistent 3 mm thickness. Brown the meat first for better flavour, though you can skip this and still get a good result with a longer cook.

Heat the oven to 170 C / fan 150 C / gas 3. Season the lamb chops. Layer the chops, kidneys (if using), onions, and carrot in a deep oven-proof dish. Tuck the thyme and bay between the layers. Pour over the stock and Worcestershire sauce.
Arrange the potato slices on top, overlapping them like roof tiles. Season well. Brush generously with melted butter.

Cover tightly with foil or a lid. Bake for 2 hours. Remove the cover, increase the heat to 200 C / fan 180 C / gas 6, and bake for a further 30 minutes until the potatoes are golden and crisp. Rest for 10 minutes before serving with pickled red cabbage.
